<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

Auth is already two-phase (`auth::stage` → `StagedAuth::publish`) and `boot::serve` binds before publishing, with a comment stating the invariant. The observed clobber therefore comes from a path that does not honour it (the --json/sandbox boot at boot.rs:207-224 stages into a directory that may resolve to the global config dir; or a staged NamedTempFile promoted on an error path; or a bind on a different address family succeeding). t1 finds it by test, t2 closes it structurally: publish is only reachable from a bound listener (make publish take the bound listener, or a proof token from bind). The 401 hint gets an mtime-vs-boot check. A prod-owner designation (env or config) refuses the prod database from foreign cwds — the cheapest defence against another government's default-config daemon.

## Risks

| risk-1 | the clobber path may be the --json sandbox boot writing into the global dir when FS3_CONFIG_DIR is unset — t1 decides; do not fix before reproducing |
